plan: This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the weakly dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $31.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so there's no advantage to bidding above or below my true value of $37. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay. I'll bid my true value of $37.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value ensures I never overpay (I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, which will be less than my value) and never miss out on profitable wins. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth to me if the second-highest bid exceeds my value. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $11, so I will bid $11.
